Search the opencode source code to find where models (especially gemini and nvidia models) are defined. Look in:
1. The opencode binary/package location - check `which opencode` to find it
2. Any config files or source files that define available models
3. Search for "gemini" and "nvidia" in the opencode installation directory

Return the exact file paths and line numbers where these models are defined, and what the surrounding code looks like so I can understand how to disable/remove them.
Now let me check the actual config files and which binary is really in use:

I have everything needed. Here is the complete report.

## Summary

opencode on this machine is distributed as **compiled Bun single-file binaries** (no JS/TS source tree exists). The model catalog is **not defined in config files** — it comes from two places in the binary itself plus a runtime-fetched cache file. There is no source-level "model registry file" to edit; the supported way to disable gemini/nvidia models is via `opencode.json` config knobs (details at the end).

---

## 2. Where the models are defined

### A. Runtime-fetched registry (primary source)

Found in the embedded JS of `/home/arc/.opencode/bin/opencode` at **byte offset ~103,493,000** – the `ModelsDev` service:

```js
t=ge.OPENCODE_MODELS_URL||"https://models.opencode.ai",
a=Wr.join(v.Path.cache,t==="https://models.opencode.ai"?"models.json":`models-${pi.fast(t)}.json`),
c=me.minutes(5),                                 // cache fresh-check TTL
...
s=n.fn("ModelsDev.fetchApi")(function*(){return yield*G.get(`${t}/api.json`)...}),
...
m=n.gen(function*(){
  let w=yield*f;                                  // 1) read cache file models.json
  if(w)return w;
  let T=yield*p;                                  // 2) built-in fallback (see B below)
  if(T)return T;
  if(ge.OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH)return{};   // 3) env-var kill switch
  ...fetch api.json and cache it...
})
```

- It fetches `https://models.opencode.ai/api.json`, caches to `~/cache/opencode/models.json`, then **re-fetches every 60 minutes** at startup (`n.forkScoped(x().pipe(n.repeat(ye.spaced("60 minutes"))))`).
- **The actual cache file on this machine: `/home/arc/.cache/opencode/models.json`** (4,490,870 B, refreshed today 10:49). It holds **213 providers**:
  - `"google"` provider (with env `["GOOGLE_API_KEY", "GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY", "GEMINI_API_KEY"]`) — starts at **byte 1,885,292**... correction: `"google"` at **byte 2,011,088**; 39 models, of which **30 are `gemini-*`**.
  - `"nvidia"` provider (with `env:["NVIDIA_API_KEY"]`) — starts at **byte 1,885,292**; **103 models** (`nemotron-*`, qwen-on-nvidia, etc.).

### B. Built-in fallback registry (bundled inside the binary)

The binary embeds the **entire models.dev dataset** as one giant minified JS object literal `p=n.sync(()=>({...}))` starting near **byte 99,529,000** of `/home/arc/.opencode/bin/opencode`. It is used when the cache file is missing and before hitting the network. Exact definition sites:

| Entity | Binary byte offset in `/home/arc/.opencode/bin/opencode` | Code snippet (embedded JS) |
|---|---|---|
| nvidia provider def | `101,202,963` (`NVIDIA_API_KEY`), `101,203,025` (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`) | `nvidia:{id:"nvidia",env:["NVIDIA_API_KEY"],npm:"@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",api:"https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1",name:"Nvidia",doc:"https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/",models:{...103 models...}}` |
| first nvidia model entry | `99,758,000` onward | `"nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:thinking":{id:"nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:thinking",name:"Nvidia Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B Thinking"...}` |
| `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning` | `99,761,176` | `"nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning":{id:"nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning",name:"Nvidia Nemotron 3.5 Lightning"...}` |
| google provider def | `101,315,055` (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`), `101,315,103` (`GEMINI_API_KEY`) | `google:{id:"google",env:["GOOGLE_API_KEY","GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY","GEMINI_API_KEY"],npm:"@ai-sdk/google",name:"Google",doc:"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models",models:{...39 models...}}` |
| `"google/gemini-pro-latest"` | `99,778,230` | `"google/gemini-pro-latest":{id:"google/gemini-pro-latest",name:"Gemini Pro Latest"...}` |
| `"google/gemini-2.5-flash"` | `100,068,490` | `"google/gemini-2.5-flash":{id:"google/gemini-2.5-flash"...}` |
| `gemini-3.8-flash` (in google provider) | `101,331,631` | `"gemini-3.8-flash":{id:"gemini-3.8-flash",name:"Gemini 3.8 Flash"...}` |

(83 `gemini` matches and 5+ `nvidia` clusters total in the binary — all inside this bundled registry + provider SDK glue.)

### C. The config schema + filtering logic (how to disable)

Config schema definition, embedded at **byte 104,366,000–104,370,000**:

```js
disabled_providers:D.optional(D.mutable(D.Array(D.String)))
  .annotate({description:"Disable providers that are loaded automatically"}),
enabled_providers:D.optional(D.mutable(D.Array(D.String)))
  .annotate({description:"When set, ONLY these providers will be enabled. All other providers will be ignored"}),
provider:D.optional(D.Record(D.String, ProviderConfig))
  .annotate({description:"Custom provider configurations and model overrides"})
```
`ProviderConfig` (at 104,361,000) includes `whitelist`, `blacklist`, and `models` fields.

Filter logic (which models actually surface in `/models`):
- Provider-level exclude, at **binary byte 96,084,000**:
  ```js
  let $=new Set(B.disabled_providers??[]),h=B.enabled_providers?new Set(B.enabled_providers):void 0;
  for(let[q,N]of Object.entries(G)) if((h?h.has(q):!0)&&!$.has(q)) z[q]=N;
  ```
- Model-level filter within a provider, at **binary byte 98,403,227**:
  ```js
  if(C.status==="alpha"&&!G.enableExperimentalModels) delete s.models[r];
  if(C.status==="deprecated") delete s.models[r];
  if(p?.blacklist&&p.blacklist.includes(r) || p?.whitelist&&!p.whitelist.includes(r))
      delete s.models[r];
  ```

## 3. How to disable/remove gemini & nvidia models

**The active config file on this machine is `/home/arc/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`** (currently contains only `"skills"`). Add one of these:

**Option 1 – Disable whole providers (simplest, recommended):**
```jsonc
{
  "disabled_providers": ["google", "nvidia"]
}
```
This removes all 39 google models (30 gemini) and all 103 nvidia models from the model list/catalog.

**Option 2 – Allowlist only the providers you want:**
```jsonc
{
  "enabled_providers": ["anthropic", "openai", "openrouter"]
}
```

**Option 3 – Per-provider model filtering (keep google, drop only gemini, or vice-versa):**
```jsonc
{
  "provider": {
    "google": { "blacklist": ["gemini-3.8-flash", "gemini-3.7-flash"] },
    "nvidia": { "blacklist": ["nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b"] }
  }
}
```
(`blacklist`/`whitelist` entries match model IDs as they appear in the registry, e.g. `nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:thinking`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, etc.)

**Option 4 – Stop the runtime fetch entirely (env var):**
`OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1` — the code path `if(ge.OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH)return{}` (binary byte 103,493,506) makes it use only the bundled fallback (which still contains gemini/nvidia) or config-defined models. Pair this with editing the cache file below.

**Option 5 – Edit the runtime cache directly:**
Edit `/home/arc/.cache/opencode/models.json` and delete the `"google":{...}` (byte 2,011,088) and `"nvidia":{...}` (byte 1,885,292) objects. **Caveat:** this file is re-fetched at startup and every 60 minutes, so the edit is not durable unless combined with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1`.

**Important:** Removing them from the binary itself is not practical — there is no source tree (the npm package contains only compiled binaries), and the model data is minified JS inside a bun executable; patching it would break the bundle. The intended, supported mechanism is the config knobs in Option 1–3 above.
